title: The Song of the Reed: The Opening of Rumi's Masnavi
subtitle: Eight Persian Sufi poems with English translation
yt_title: The Song of the Reed | Rumi's Masnavi Opening in Persian with English Translation
intro: The Masnavi, Rumi's great poem, opens with a reed flute crying for the reed bed it was cut from.
Persians call these lines the Ney-nameh, the Book of the Reed. Many know them by heart.
Here are eight passages from that opening song, with a few words on each.

poems.name: Every Gathering

lines.fa: من به هر جمعیتی نالان شدم
lines.en: In every gathering I cried my lament;

lines.fa: جفت بدحالان و خوشحالان شدم
lines.en: I kept company with the unhappy and the happy.

lines.fa: هر کسی از ظن خود شد یار من
lines.en: Each became my friend from their own guess;

lines.fa: از درون من نجست اسرار من
lines.en: none sought out the secrets within me.

tafsir: The reed plays at weddings and at funerals, for the sad and for the glad.
Everyone loves its music. Everyone hears in it what they already feel.
But almost no one asks what the reed itself is crying about.
Many people know this loneliness: to be liked, and not known.

poems.name: Not Far From My Cry

lines.fa: سر من از ناله من دور نیست
lines.en: My secret is not far from my lament,

lines.fa: لیک چشم و گوش را آن نور نیست
lines.en: but eye and ear do not have that light.

tafsir: The reed's secret is right there in its sound.
It is not hidden. We simply do not have the light to see it.
Ordinary eyes and ears hear only notes.
Another kind of seeing is needed: the eye of the heart.

poems.name: This Cry Is Fire

lines.fa: آتش است این بانگ نای و نیست باد
lines.en: This cry of the reed is fire, not wind;

lines.fa: هر که این آتش ندارد نیست باد
lines.en: whoever does not have this fire, may they be nothing.

lines.fa: آتش عشق است کاندر نی فتاد
lines.en: It is the fire of love that fell into the reed;

lines.fa: جوشش عشق است کاندر می فتاد
lines.en: it is the ferment of love that fell into the wine.

tafsir: A flute is played with breath, with wind.
Rumi says: no, this sound is fire.
The same love that makes the reed cry makes the wine ferment.
Without that fire, he says, a life is hardly a life.

poems.name: Poison and Antidote

lines.fa: نی حریف هر که از یاری برید
lines.en: The reed is the companion of all who are cut off from a friend;

lines.fa: پرده‌هایش پرده‌های ما درید
lines.en: its melodies tore open our veils.

lines.fa: همچو نی زهری و تریاقی که دید
lines.en: Who has seen a poison and an antidote like the reed?

lines.fa: همچو نی دمساز و مشتاقی که دید
lines.en: Who has seen a companion and a lover like the reed?

tafsir: In Persian, the same word, parde, means a musical mode and a veil.
So the reed's melodies tear the veils that cover our hearts.
Its music wounds and heals at the same time.
Anyone separated from someone they love has found a friend in this sound.

poems.name: The Road Full of Blood

lines.fa: نی حدیث راه پرخون می‌کند
lines.en: The reed tells of the road full of blood;

lines.fa: قصه‌های عشق مجنون می‌کند
lines.en: it tells the stories of Majnun's love.

tafsir: Majnun is the great lover of Persian and Arabic legend, driven mad by his love for Layla.
His road was hard, full of wounds.
The reed sings that story.
Love, in Rumi, is never a comfortable road. But it is the one worth taking.

poems.name: The Fish and the Water

lines.fa: هر که جز ماهی ز آبش سیر شد
lines.en: Everyone but the fish grows tired of water;

lines.fa: هر که بی‌روزیست روزش دیر شد
lines.en: for whoever lacks their daily bread, the day grows long.

tafsir: A fish never has enough water. It lives in it.
Rumi says the true lover is like that with love.
Others grow bored, and for them the days drag on.
The one who has found their element does not count the hours.

poems.name: When the Rose Is Gone

lines.fa: چون که گل رفت و گلستان درگذشت
lines.en: When the rose is gone and the garden has faded,

lines.fa: نشنوی زآن پس ز بلبل سرگذشت
lines.en: you will hear no more the nightingale's story.

tafsir: The nightingale sings because of the rose.
Take away the rose, and the song stops.
Rumi is speaking of himself, and of Shams, who was his rose.
Our deepest songs need someone to sing to.

poems.name: All Is the Beloved

lines.fa: جمله معشوق است و عاشق پرده‌ای
lines.en: All is the Beloved; the lover is only a veil.

lines.fa: زنده معشوق است و عاشق مرده‌ای
lines.en: The Beloved is the living one; the lover is a dead thing.

tafsir: Here the song of the reed reaches its deepest point.
In the end, Rumi says, there is only the Beloved.
The lover is a curtain, and all the life is on the other side.
This is the secret the reed has been crying about all along.
